title: Review: Mass spectrometry of elements; Empirical and molecular formulae; States of matter and phase changes; Photoelectron spectroscopy and Coulomb's law (AP); Orbitals and electron configuration; Ionization energies; Periodic table structure and blocks
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BD08#t1 term and clue written for the game; BD08#t3 term and clue written for the game; AS04#t3 term and clue written for the game; AS04#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM02#N.3, AS02#N.6c, AS04#N.12b, AS05#N.11, AS07#N.2, BD08#N.11, PT01#N.12a, AM02#N.7b, AS02#N.6b, AS04#N.6b, AS05#N.4b, AS07#N.12. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Sublimation
items.clue: Change of state directly from solid to gas.

items.label: Evaporation
items.clue: Liquid turns to gas at the surface only, at any temperature.

items.label: Orbital
items.clue: A region around the nucleus where an electron is likely to be found; not a path.

questions.stem: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. Its molar mass is 60.05 g/mol. What is the empirical formula of the compound?

options.text: CH₂O
C₆HO₈
CHO
C₂H₄O₂

questions.explanation: In 100 g: 3.33 mol C, about 6.6–6.7 mol H, 3.33 mol O. ÷ smallest: 1 : 2 : 1.

questions.stem: A laboratory prepares a sample of magnesium in which the proportions of the three isotopes of magnesium differ from those in natural magnesium. Which information is needed to calculate the average atomic mass of magnesium in this sample?

options.text: The masses of all three isotopes and the number of isotopes
The atomic mass given for magnesium on the periodic table
The mass of the isotope giving the tallest mass-spectrum peak
The mass and the relative abundance of each isotope in the sample

questions.explanation: Multiply each isotope's mass by its fractional abundance in this sample, then add.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the electrons in a ground-state magnesium atom, 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s²?

options.text: They move on fixed circular paths, one path for each subshell, at set distances from the nucleus.
The two 3s electrons are core electrons, since the 3s subshell is full.
They occupy subshells of different energies; the two 3s electrons are the valence electrons.
All twelve are in the third shell, because magnesium is in period 3.

questions.explanation: The 3s electrons are, on average, farthest from the nucleus and need the least energy to remove.

questions.stem: Element X is in Period 3. Its first six ionization energies are 1012, 1907, 2914, 4964, 6274 and 21 268 kJ/mol. Which statement identifies X and explains the large sixth value?

options.text: X is sulfur: the jump is at the sixth ionisation energy, so X has six outer electrons.
X is phosphorus: the sixth electron is the first from the second shell, nearer the nucleus.
X is phosphorus: the sixth electron would come from a full shell, which is especially stable.
X is aluminium: the rise from 2914 to 4964 is where a new shell starts.

questions.explanation: Five electrons come from the third shell. The sixth comes from 2p: much closer to the nucleus, much less shielded, so held far more strongly.

questions.stem: Two particles with charges of +2 and −2 are separated by a distance d and attract each other with a force of magnitude F. Two other particles, with charges of +2 and −1, are separated by a distance of d/2. What is the magnitude of the force between the second pair of particles?
questions.explanation: Product of charges halved (4 → 2); 1/r² multiplied by 4. Force = (1/2)(4)F = 2.00F.

questions.stem: The molar enthalpy of vaporization of water at 100 °C is 40.7 kJ/mol. How much energy is released when 1.60 g of steam at 100 °C condenses to liquid water at 100 °C?
questions.explanation: n = 1.60 ÷ 18.02 = 0.0888 mol. Condensing releases what vaporizing absorbs: 0.0888 × 40.7 = 3.61 kJ.

questions.stem: Beryllium, 1s² 2s², and helium, 1s², both have two electrons in their outer s sub-shell. Why is beryllium placed in group 2, but helium in group 18?

options.text: Beryllium is a solid and helium is a gas, and group 18 holds the gaseous elements.
Beryllium has four electrons and helium two, and the group number counts the total.
Beryllium's 2s² electrons are in a higher shell, so they are inner electrons, not valence electrons.
Beryllium's outer shell, n = 2, is far from full, while helium's n = 1 shell is full with just two.

questions.stem: A student has found the empirical formula of a molecular compound from its percent composition by mass. Which additional quantity does the student need in order to determine the compound's molecular formula?

options.text: None; the empirical formula is also the molecular formula
The total mass of the sample of the compound analyzed
The molar mass of the compound, found by another method
The atomic numbers of the elements in the compound

questions.explanation: Molar mass ÷ empirical formula mass gives the whole-number multiple.

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of a sample of a hypothetical element Z shows three peaks, with heights given relative to the tallest peak: 28 amu (100), 29 amu (8.0) and 30 amu (4.0). What is the average atomic mass of Z in the sample, in amu?
A student writes the electron configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶3d³ for a ground-state scandium atom, which has 21 electrons. Which statement correctly evaluates the student's configuration?

options.text: It is the ground state: subshells fill in order of shell number, so 3d is filled before 4s.
It is not the ground state: the third shell is full with 8 electrons, so the last three are 4s²4p¹.
It is not the ground state: 4s fills before 3d, so the last three electrons are 4s²3d¹.
It is not the ground state: d subshells begin in the fourth shell, so the last three are 4s²4d¹.

questions.explanation: After 3p, 4s fills, and the 21st electron enters 3d: …4s²3d¹.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the process whose energy change is the first ionization energy of magnesium?

options.text: An atom in solid Mg loses two electrons, forming an aqueous Mg²⁺ ion
An atom in solid Mg loses one electron, forming a gaseous Mg⁺ ion
A gaseous Mg atom takes in one electron, forming a gaseous Mg⁻ ion
A gaseous Mg atom loses one electron, forming a gaseous Mg⁺ ion

questions.explanation: One electron removed from an isolated gaseous atom in its ground state.

questions.stem: The complete photoelectron spectrum of an element has six peaks. From highest to lowest binding energy, their relative heights are 2, 2, 6, 2, 6 and 1. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The element is argon; the right-hand peak shows its outermost 3p electron.
The element is potassium; the right-hand peak is shortest because its electron needs the least energy.
The element is potassium; its 4s electron is farthest out and shielded by 18 core electrons.
The element is calcium; it has six occupied subshells, so its spectrum has six peaks.

questions.explanation: Heights add to 19 electrons: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s¹. The 4s electron is far from the nucleus with Zeff ≈ +1, so its peak is at the lowest binding energy.
